text:
Sam: Heads-up - UX review for the metrics chart. Main things: legend placement (right vs overlay), axis unit toggling (auto vs explicit), smoothing control location, and outlier handling strategy. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/metrics-ui-xyz

Zoe: Quick take: right-side legend eats horizontal space on narrow dashboards. Overlay pill works but we lose immediate mapping. What if we do a small inline legend that collapses names but keeps swatches + short abbreviations (e.g., CPU -> CPU%)?

Lena: Abbrev helps but leaks domain knowledge. For units: should the axis show "requests/s" or "req/s"? We have mixed uses. Consistency matters for non-dev stakeholders. My vote: prefer human-readable full units where space allows, fallback to abbreviated unit with tooltip showing full label.

Priya: Accessibility note: when unit toggles dynamically (auto units scale: K, M), screen readers need to hear the unit change. Add aria-live region for axis unit updates. Also ensure formatted values have accessible text: e.g., visually "1.2K" but screenreader reads "1,200 requests per second".

Miguel: Implementation details:
- We already have a formatter util with `formatNumber(value, {style: 'compact'})`.
- Add `formatNumberAccessible` that returns long form for `aria-label`.
- Legend: overlay popover is easiest, but we must avoid clipping on small panels. Could fall back to inline stacked legend under the chart when height permits.

Sam: Good. Outliers: product asked for auto-clamp with a "+outliers" marker for points outside y-axis. Design wants to show them rather than hide. Thoughts?

Zoe: Show them but visually de-emphasize (thin stroke, lighter opacity) and add a small label `+n outliers` at the top edge. Clicking the label expands the y-axis to include them. This keeps context while avoiding axis inflation.

Lena: +1. Also offer an explicit toggle in chart settings: "Include outliers in scale" (off by default for overview dashboards). Copy: "Exclude extreme values from axis to preserve trend visibility. Click to include." Short and clear.

Priya: A11y for outlier label: make it focusable and announce how many outliers are hidden or shown. Screenreader copy example: "Three points excluded from scale. Press Enter to include in chart."

Miguel: Smoothing: analytics show users rarely change smoothing per-chart; it's usually a global preference. Suggest moving smoothing switch into chart toolbar dropdown (advanced) not the primary legend. Default should be off for latency and perf charts.

Sam: Decision proposal:
1) Legend: default inline compact (swatch + abbrev) on >=720px, overlay pill on <720px, stacked drawer fallback if overlay clips.
2) Units: show full human-readable units when space available, fallback to abbreviated K/M with tooltip showing expanded text. Add aria-label with long form values.
3) Outliers: visually de-emphasize outliers and show "+n outliers" affordance to expand the axis; add chart setting toggle to include by default.
4) Smoothing: move to toolbar advanced controls; default off for perf dashboards.

Can design + eng ack these and sign off?

Zoe: I'll update Figma with compact legend and outlier badge variants.

Miguel: I'll prototype formatNumberAccessible and add aria-live hook for unit/scale changes.

Priya: I'll draft the exact screenreader strings and QA checklist (keyboard focus order, aria-live testing, tooltip visibility).

qa-bot: Reminder: visual regression tests will run on the branch once the figma spec is linked in PR body.

Sam: Thanks team. Let's target next week's sprint for the prototype + accessibility QA. :rocket:
